replacement_semantics: When no source is eligible for a target stratum, the predecessor adds the whole target-stratum share to uncovered. When some planned sources are ineligible but at least one is eligible, it renormalizes weights onto eligible survivors, assigns no uncovered mass to the excluded present source, and can emit a complete distribution. The repaired candidate instead computes the denominator over all planned sources, retains proportional missing_share, and adds that mass to uncovered. Thus for partial ineligibility the predecessor can have zero uncovered mass while the repaired candidate has positive uncovered mass. F6P's excluded-source-with-zero-uncovered FALSE_FULL_COVERAGE check is the relevant downstream risk. This is static source reasoning, not an executed scientific result.
